statement: The supplied sources do not contain a derivation of the chain rule, as the proof section terminates prematurely after introducing the difference quotient. By definition, the chain rule is a formula expressing the derivative of the composition of differentiable functions: for composite differentiable functions y = f(u) and u = g(x), the derivative at x = a is given by (f ∘ g)'(a) = f'(g(a)) · g'(a), or in Leibniz notation, dy/dx = (dy/du) · (du/dx). For a three-function composition y = f(u), u = g(v), v = h(x), (f ∘ g ∘ h)'(a) = f'((g ∘ h)(a)) · g'(h(a)) · h'(a) = (f' ∘ g ∘ h)(a) · (g' ∘ h)(a) · h'(a), or dy/dx = (dy/du) · (du/dv) · (dv/dx).

properties.why: obtained by rewriting f(x)/g(x) as f(x) · (1/g(x)) and combining the product rule with the chain rule applied to the reciprocal function 1/x

properties.property: Derivative of inverse functions: f'(y) = 1 / g'(f(y)) where x = f(y) is the inverse of y = g(x)
properties.why: obtained by differentiating both sides of the identity f(g(x)) = x via the chain rule to get f'(g(x))g'(x) = 1 and substituting x = f(y)

properties.property: Arbitrary n-fold composition rule: D f_{1..n} = ∏_{k=1}^n [D f_k ∘ f_{(k+1)..n}], or f'_{1..n}(x) = ∏_{k=1}^n f'_k(f_{(k+1..n)}(x))
properties.why: follows from associative grouping and repeated application of the chain rule to a chain of n differentiable functions

properties.property: Higher derivatives (Faà di Bruno's formula): d^2y/dx^2 = (d^2y/du^2)(du/dx)^2 + (dy/du)(d^2u/dx^2)
properties.why: obtained by differentiating the first-order chain rule dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx) using the product rule and chain rule
forms the mathematical basis of the backpropagation algorithm used for gradient descent in deep neural networks

assumptions.assumption: Constituent functions are differentiable at the corresponding points of composition evaluation
assumptions.breaks_when: Any component function or its inverse fails to be differentiable at the required intermediate evaluation point

failure_modes.mode: Division by zero in inverse function derivative formula
failure_modes.cause: The derivative g'(f(y)) equals zero, meaning the inverse function f is not differentiable at y (e.g., g(x) = x^3 at x = 0 with inverse f(y) = y^(1/3))

failure_modes.signature: Derivative is undefined or expression cannot be evaluated
failure_modes.cause: A component function is non-differentiable at the value produced by the preceding function in the chain
